newsitem.title: USA: Nobel economics winner Vickrey dies -- university.
newsitem.headline: Nobel economics winner Vickrey dies -- university.

text.p: William Vickrey, who was a co-winner of the 1996 Nobel Prize for Economics three days ago, died on Friday after suffering a heart attack at the wheel of his car, a Columbia University spokeswoman said.
He was driving to a conference in Boston when he suffered the attack on Thursday night and was pronounced dead early Friday, the spokeswoman said.
Spokeswoman Anne Canty said colleagues were deeply saddened at the death of the 82-year-old scholar but added: "We're pleased that his work was publicly recognised before he died".
Vickrey and British professor James Mirrlees won the prize, worth a total $1.12 million, for their separate contributions "to the economic theory of incentives under asymmetric information."
The research of both focused on how organisations could make competent decisions based on incomplete -- or asymmetric -- information.
The Canadian-born Vickrey spent his career crusading for innovative solutions to common economic problems of taxation, utilities and urban transportation.
